name: Alacritty
description: Dark and light Alacritty color files: ANSI colors (normal, bright and dim) plus cursor, vi-mode, selection, search, hints and footer bar.
install:
Copy `termicolor-dark.toml` (or `-light`) next to your config, e.g. `~/.config/alacritty/`
(`%APPDATA%\alacritty\` on Windows), and import it from `alacritty.toml`:

```toml
[general]
import = ["~/.config/alacritty/termicolor-dark.toml"]
```

Alacritty reloads the config live.
Needs Alacritty 0.13+ (TOML config).

name: bat
description: TextMate themes for bat, also used by git-delta, plus a delta config with matching diff colors.
install:
### bat

```sh
mkdir -p "$(bat --config-dir)/themes"
cp termicolor-dark.tmTheme termicolor-light.tmTheme "$(bat --config-dir)/themes/"
bat cache --build
bat --list-themes | grep -i termicolor
```

Then pick the theme in `$(bat --config-file)` (or with `BAT_THEME`):

```sh
--theme="termicolor-dark"
```

bat 0.25+ can follow the terminal's background instead:

```sh
--theme="auto"
--theme-dark="termicolor-dark"
--theme-light="termicolor-light"
```

On Windows, `bat --config-dir` is usually `%APPDATA%\bat`. Run the same copy and `bat cache --build` steps.

### git-delta

[delta](https://github.com/dandavison/delta) reads bat's theme cache, so install the bat themes first
(`delta --list-syntax-themes` should then list them). Copy `delta.gitconfig` somewhere stable
(e.g. `~/.config/delta/termicolor.gitconfig`) and include it from `~/.gitconfig`:

```ini
[include]
    path = ~/.config/delta/termicolor.gitconfig

[core]
    pager = delta

[interactive]
    diffFilter = delta --color-only

[delta]
    features = termicolor-dark
    navigate = true
    # line-numbers = true
    # side-by-side = true

[merge]
    conflictStyle = zdiff3

[diff]
    colorMoved = default
```

Use `features = termicolor-light` on a light terminal. Each feature sets `syntax-theme`, the
added/removed line and word backgrounds, line numbers, hunk headers, blame and merge-conflict styles.

name: btop
description: Resource monitor themes covering every btop theme key, graphs and meters included.
install:
Copy the theme files to the user themes folder:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/btop/themes   # or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/btop/themes
cp termicolor-dark.theme termicolor-light.theme ~/.config/btop/themes/
```

Then select one in `~/.config/btop/btop.conf`:

```ini
color_theme = "termicolor-dark"
theme_background = True
truecolor = True
```

Or pick it live from the options menu (`o`, then *Color theme*). Set `theme_background = False` to keep
your terminal's own background.

name: Chrome & Edge
description: Browser frame, tab strip, toolbar and new tab page colors for Chromium browsers.
install:
1. Open `chrome://extensions` (or `edge://extensions`) and enable **Developer mode**.
2. **Load unpacked** → select `dist/dark` or `dist/light`.

Chrome keeps one theme at a time; loading the other replaces it.

name: fzf
description: Fuzzy finder colors as FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS snippets for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell.
install:
Copy the files you need to `~/.config/fzf/` (any folder works, adjust the paths below).
Each snippet appends `--color` options to `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS`, so load it after anything else that sets it.
Use the `-light` files on a light terminal.

**bash / zsh:** add to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`:

```sh
source ~/.config/fzf/fzf-dark.sh
```

**fish:** add to `~/.config/fish/config.fish`:

```fish
source ~/.config/fzf/fzf-dark.fish
```

**PowerShell:** add to `$PROFILE`:

```powershell
. "$HOME\.config\fzf\fzf-dark.ps1"
```

**Any shell (fzf 0.48+):** point `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE` at `fzf-dark.opts`, which holds the bare options:

```sh
export FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE=~/.config/fzf/fzf-dark.opts
```

Newer color names (`ghost`, `footer`) need a recent fzf. Older releases reject names they don't know,
so upgrade fzf or delete those entries.

name: Ghostty
description: Dark and light Ghostty themes: ANSI palette plus cursor, selection, search, splits and titlebar.
install:
Copy `termicolor-dark` and `termicolor-light` into `~/.config/ghostty/themes/`
(`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ghostty/themes/` if set), then in your Ghostty config:

```ini
theme = light:termicolor-light,dark:termicolor-dark
```

Or pin one with `theme = termicolor-dark`. Reload with *Reload Configuration* (`cmd+shift+,` / `ctrl+shift+,`).
The search colors apply to Ghostty's in-terminal search (1.3+); older versions warn about them and ignore them.

name: GNOME Terminal
description: Dark and light profiles for GNOME Terminal, installed through gsettings or dconf.
install:
**Script:** run `install.sh` to add *Termicolor Dark* and *Termicolor Light* profiles:

```sh
bash install.sh                 # both profiles
bash install.sh dark --default   # one profile, made the default
```

Re-running it updates the same profiles in place. Pick a profile in *Preferences* or from the
new-tab menu.

**dconf:** load a single profile by hand, then add its id to the profile list
(`org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList list`) so it shows up:

```sh
dconf load /org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:46edc057-d8e6-4aa1-a6a2-3b83272ead24/ < termicolor-dark.dconf
```

The light profile's id is `5c7f0537-5c7f-4f86-8e09-fadd0a973257`.

name: iTerm2
description: Color presets for the iTerm2 macOS terminal, plus a combined preset that follows the system light/dark appearance.
install:
1. Open *Settings → Profiles → Colors*.
2. Click **Color Presets… → Import…** and pick `termicolor-dark.itermcolors` (and/or `termicolor-light.itermcolors`).
3. Choose the imported preset from the same menu.

**Follow the system appearance:** tick *Use separate colors for light and dark mode* in the Colors tab,
then import and select `termicolor.itermcolors`. It carries both modes in one preset.

name: kitty
description: Dark and light kitty themes: ANSI colors plus cursor, selection, borders, tab bar and marks.
install:
**Theme kitten:** copy `termicolor-dark.conf` and `termicolor-light.conf` into `~/.config/kitty/themes/`,
then run `kitten themes` and pick *Termicolor Dark* (it's listed under *user-defined*), or apply it directly:

```sh
kitten themes "Termicolor Dark"
```

**Follow the OS light/dark setting:** copy the files into the kitty config folder as
`dark-theme.auto.conf` and `light-theme.auto.conf` (on GNOME also copy the light one as
`no-preference-theme.auto.conf`), then restart kitty.

**Manual:** add `include termicolor-dark.conf` to `~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf`.

name: lazygit
description: Git TUI theme: borders, selection, cherry-pick and rebase markers.
install:
Merge one of the files into your lazygit `config.yml`:

| OS      | Path                                              |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Linux   | `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml`                  |
| macOS   | `~/Library/Application Support/lazygit/config.yml` |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lazygit\config.yml`             |

- `lazygit-dark.yml` / `lazygit-light.yml` set `gui.theme` for one mode.
- `lazygit-auto.yml` sets `gui.darkTheme` and `gui.lightTheme`, and lazygit picks one from the terminal's
  background (`gui.colorScheme: auto`). Needs a lazygit recent enough to have those keys.

To keep the theme in its own file, layer it over your config instead of copying it in:

```sh
export LG_CONFIG_FILE="$HOME/.config/lazygit/config.yml,$HOME/.config/lazygit/lazygit-dark.yml"
```

name: LS_COLORS
description: Truecolor LS_COLORS for ls, eza, fd, tree and other tools that read it, plus an eza theme.yml for permissions, sizes and git columns.
install:
**dircolors (bash/zsh):** save `termicolor-dark.dircolors` (or `-light`) as `~/.dircolors` and add to your rc file:

```sh
eval "$(dircolors -b ~/.dircolors)"
```

**No dircolors** (macOS without coreutils, fish, or just simpler): source the prebuilt string instead,
`ls-colors-dark.sh` from bash/zsh or `ls-colors-dark.fish` from `config.fish`. GNU `ls` needs
`--color=auto`; BSD/macOS `ls` ignores `LS_COLORS`, but eza, fd, lsd and tree read it.

**eza:** copy `eza-dark.yml` (or `-light`) to `~/.config/eza/theme.yml` (or `$EZA_CONFIG_DIR/theme.yml`).
It colors permissions, sizes, users, dates and git status. `LS_COLORS` / `EZA_COLORS` win where they
overlap, so keep the two in the same mode.

All colors are 24-bit; use a truecolor terminal.

name: PowerShell PSReadLine
description: Command-line syntax colors for PowerShell (PSReadLine), in dark and light.
install:
1. Save `termicolor-dark.ps1` (or `-light`) somewhere, for example next to your profile.
2. Open your profile (`notepad $PROFILE`, or `code $PROFILE`) and dot-source it:

    ```powershell
    . "$HOME\Documents\PowerShell\termicolor-dark.ps1"
    ```

3. Restart the shell.

Prediction colors are only set where your PSReadLine supports them (2.1+ inline, 2.2+ list view).
Windows PowerShell 5.1 ships PSReadLine 2.0; `Install-Module PSReadLine -Force` gets the current one.
Pair it with a Termicolor terminal scheme (e.g. Windows Terminal) for matching ANSI colors.

name: Shiki & Monaco
description: Syntax highlighting themes for shiki (and Monaco via @shikijs/monaco). Same token rules as VS Code.

name: Starship
description: Palette blocks and a rainbow powerline preset for the Starship prompt.
install:
**Full preset:** copy `starship-dark.toml` (or `-light`) to `~/.config/starship.toml`.
Needs a [Nerd Font](https://www.nerdfonts.com).

**Palette only:** append `palettes.toml` to your config and set `palette = 'termicolor_dark'`.
Colors: `red orange yellow green cyan blue purple pink` for text, `fill_<accent>` for solid segments
with `on_fill_<accent>` text on them, and `text subtext surface base crust` for neutrals.

name: Visual Studio Code
description: Dark and light color themes for VS Code and VSCodium, matching repraze.com code blocks.
install:
Not on the Marketplace yet. Package and install the extension folder:

```sh
cd ports/vscode/dist
npx @vscode/vsce package -o termicolor.vsix
code --install-extension termicolor.vsix
```

Then pick **Termicolor Dark** or **Termicolor Light** in *Preferences: Color Theme*.

name: Wallpapers
description: Abstract generated wallpapers: gradients, lines and patterns in the palette, dark and light. Seeded, reproducible SVG.
install:
**Easiest:** pick one in the gallery below and download it as **JPG** (the default) at 1080p, QHD or 4K. It's
rendered at full size in your browser. JPG works as a wallpaper everywhere, Windows included. Then right-click it,
and choose *Set as desktop background* (Windows), or set it in your desktop's settings.

**From the repo:** pick a file under `dist/<mode>/<width>x<height>/`: landscape `1920x1080`, `2560x1440`, `3840x2160` or portrait
`1080x1920`, `1440x2560`, `2160x3840`. Portrait files have their own layout, not a crop of landscape.
`catalog.json` lists every wallpaper with its generator, seed and parameters.

The repo files are SVG (small, exact, any size). To convert one yourself:
`rsvg-convert dist/dark/3840x2160/flow-2.svg -o flow-2.png` (librsvg) or Inkscape's export.

Generators, parameters and kept seeds are documented in
[`packages/wallpapers/CATALOG.md`](../../packages/wallpapers/CATALOG.md).

name: Warp
description: Dark and light custom themes for the Warp terminal.
install:
1. Copy `termicolor_dark.yaml` and `termicolor_light.yaml` into Warp's themes folder (create it if missing):
    - macOS: `~/.warp/themes/`
    - Linux: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/warp-terminal/themes/`
    - Windows: `%APPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\themes\`
2. Restart Warp, then pick **Termicolor Dark** or **Termicolor Light** in *Settings → Appearance → Themes*.

To follow the OS, enable *Sync with OS* there and assign one theme to each mode.

name: WezTerm
description: Dark and light WezTerm color schemes (TOML) plus a Lua module that also themes the fancy tab bar and follows the OS appearance.
install:
**Lua module (recommended):** copy `termicolor.lua` into `~/.config/wezterm/` and add to `wezterm.lua`:

```lua
local termicolor = require("termicolor")
termicolor.apply_to_config(config) -- or termicolor.apply_to_config(config, "light")
```

It registers both schemes, picks one from the OS light/dark setting and colors the fancy tab bar
(`window_frame`). WezTerm reloads the config when the appearance changes.

**Scheme files only:** copy `colors/termicolor-dark.toml` and `colors/termicolor-light.toml` into
`~/.config/wezterm/colors/` (or a `colors` folder next to `wezterm.exe` on Windows) and set:

```lua
config.color_scheme = "Termicolor Dark"
```

name: Windows Terminal
description: Color schemes plus a matching window/tab theme for Windows Terminal.
install:
**Option A - fragment (auto-loads):** copy `termicolor.json` to
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows Terminal\Fragments\termicolor\termicolor.json` and restart.
The schemes appear in *Settings → Color schemes*.

**Option B - settings.json:** paste the objects from `schemes.json` into `"schemes"` and from
`themes.json` into `"themes"`. Then set:

```json
"profiles": {"defaults": {"colorScheme": "Termicolor Dark"}},
"theme": "Termicolor Dark"
```

name: zsh-syntax-highlighting
description: Fish-like command line highlighting for zsh, in the same syntax colors as the editor themes.
install:
Copy `termicolor-dark.zsh` (or `-light`) to `~/.config/zsh/` and source it in `~/.zshrc`, before the plugin
(which must stay the last thing sourced):

```zsh
source ~/.config/zsh/termicolor-dark.zsh
ZSH_HIGHLIGHT_HIGHLIGHTERS=(main brackets)   # optional: colored bracket levels
source /path/to/zsh-syntax-highlighting/zsh-syntax-highlighting.zsh
```

With a plugin manager, load the theme file before the plugin (oh-my-zsh: source it above `source $ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh`).

Colors are 24-bit hex, which needs zsh 5.7+ and a truecolor terminal. On a 256-color terminal, add
`zmodload zsh/nearcolor` before sourcing the theme.
